## Purpose

This procedure describes the in vitro determination of chlorophyll *a*
and pheophytin *a* concentrations in marine and freshwater phytoplankton
by fluorescence. Chlorophyll-containing cells are concentrated on a
glass fiber filter, extracted in 90% acetone, and measured on the Turner
Designs Trilogy Fluorometer before and after acidification with 0.1 N
HCl. The method is modified from US EPA Method 445.0 and APHA Standard
Methods 10200 H [@apha2012; @epa445].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Chlorophyll *a* and pheophytin *a* in surface water,
  freshwater, and marine water samples collected per
  [SOP-F300](../field_sops/SOP-F300-surface-water-sampling.qmd)
- **Does not apply to:** In vivo chlorophyll measurements with field
  multiprobes (see [SOP-F200](../field_sops/SOP-F200-eureka-manta2.qmd));
  benthic algae unless filtration volumes are adjusted; HPLC-based
  pigment analysis
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133

| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure standards are current   |

| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Acetone (HPLC grade) is highly flammable and an
  irritant. Work in the fume hood and away from ignition sources.
  Concentrated HCl is severely corrosive. 0.1 N HCl is a mild irritant.
- **Physical:** Glass filtration apparatus and cuvettes pose breakage
  risk. Sonicator tip generates heat and noise.
- **Noise:** The sonicator requires hearing protection (ear plugs or
  ear muffs) whenever it is in use.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Hearing protection (when using sonicator)

### Emergency Procedures

For acetone spills, extinguish all ignition sources, ventilate the area,
and clean up per
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For HCl splashes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Dispose of
all acetone waste in the designated organic waste collection bottle.

## Procedure

### Reagent Preparation

**0.1 N HCl:** Add 0.85 mL of concentrated HCl to approximately 50 mL
of Milli-Q water in a 100 mL volumetric flask. Bring to volume with
Milli-Q water. Mix thoroughly.

**90% Aqueous Acetone:** Measure 100 mL of Milli-Q water into a 100 mL
volumetric flask, then transfer to a 1 L volumetric flask. Fill to the
1 L mark with HPLC-grade acetone. Mix and transfer to a dark amber
bottle. Label and store in the flammables cabinet.

**Chlorophyll *a* Stock Standard Solution (SSS):** Working in subdued
light, transfer the contents of the chlorophyll *a* ampoule into a
50 mL volumetric flask and dilute to volume with 90% acetone. Determine
the concentration spectrophotometrically. Wrap in foil and label with
the lot number. Stable for at least six months in an airtight container
at room temperature.

**Primary Dilution Standard (PDS):** Add 1 mL of SSS to a 100 mL
volumetric flask and dilute to volume with 90% acetone. If the SSS was
prepared from exactly 1 mg of pure chlorophyll *a*, the PDS
concentration is 200 ug/L. Prepare fresh before use. Wrap in foil.

**Quality Control Standards (QCs):** Prepare from the PDS at the
following concentrations: 5, 20, 50, and 200 ug/L. Wrap in foil.

::: {.callout-important}
All photosynthetic pigments are light- and temperature-sensitive.
Perform all work in subdued light. Store all standards, QC materials,
and filter samples in the dark at --20 C when not in use.
:::

### Filtration

1. Invert the sample bottle gently several times to suspend particles
2. Assemble the glass filtration unit: place the fritted glass base on
   the Erlenmeyer flask, position a GF/F filter on the frit using
   forceps, seat the glass funnel on top, and secure with the spring
   clamp
3. Connect the vacuum hose and turn on the vacuum
4. Working in subdued light, filter the sample in 20 mL increments
   using a graduated cylinder. The volume required depends on algal
   density:

| Sample Type     | Typical Volume |
|:----------------|:---------------|
| Benthic samples | approximately 5 mL |
| Freshwater      | 20--300 mL     |
| Seawater        | 100--1000+ mL  |

5. Stop filtering when a brown or green tint is visible on the filter.
   Record the exact filtered volume. If the filter becomes too darkly
   colored, the sample may exceed the linear dynamic range and require
   dilution during analysis.
6. Using forceps and a micro spatula, fold the filter in half with the
   retained material on the inside
7. Gently blot excess water from the outside of the filter with a
   Kimwipe
8. Place the folded filter in a clean 15 mL centrifuge tube or a
   plastic petri dish
9. Include a laboratory reagent blank (100 mL Milli-Q water through a
   GF/F filter) and a field duplicate every 10--15 samples
10. Wrap the tubes or dishes in aluminum foil and store at --20 C.
    Filters may be stored frozen for up to 28 days before extraction.

### Extraction -- Sonication Method

1. Remove samples and QCs from the freezer and allow to reach room
   temperature
2. Add 25 mL of 90% aqueous acetone to each tube, ensuring the filter
   is fully submerged. Cap the tubes and invert several times.
3. Secure the sonicator probe in its clamp stand
4. **Put on hearing protection**
5. Set the sonicator to 70% amplitude
6. Submerge the tip halfway into the acetone solution and sonicate,
   moving the tip around the sample to break up the filter completely
7. After sonication, shake the tube vigorously, wrap in foil, and steep
   in the refrigerator (4 C) for a minimum of 2 hours

::: {.callout-important}
Never operate the sonicator outside of solution. The tip will overheat
and be damaged.
:::

### Extraction -- Tissue Grinder Method (Alternative)

1. Using forceps, transfer the filter into a 30 mL glass grinding tube
   and push it to the bottom with the pestle or a glass rod
2. Add 4 mL of 90% acetone and grind with the pestle until the filter
   is converted to a slurry. Avoid overheating.
3. Pour the slurry into a 15 mL screw-cap centrifuge tube
4. Rinse the pestle and grinding tube with 6 mL of 90% acetone and add
   the rinse to the centrifuge tube
5. Cap, shake vigorously, wrap in foil, and steep at 4 C for 2 hours
6. Clean the grinder and pestle with water followed by acetone between
   samples; wipe dry with a Kimwipe

### Post-Extraction Processing

1. Remove samples from the refrigerator and allow to reach room
   temperature (approximately 30 minutes)
2. Shake each tube vigorously
3. Centrifuge at 1,000 x g for 5 minutes using the fixed-angle rotor
   until all filter material is pelleted
4. Handle tubes carefully after centrifugation; do not resuspend the
   pellet

### Fluorometric Analysis

1. Transfer 2.5 mL of clear supernatant from each tube into a clean
   glass cuvette, taking care not to disturb the pellet
2. Turn on the Trilogy Fluorometer and allow the 10-minute warm-up to
   complete (see [SOP-L203](SOP-L203-trilogy-fluorometer.qmd))
3. Select the **Chlor-A** (Chlorophyll Acidification) module on the
   touch screen
4. Calibrate using the QCs prepared from the PDS, or load a saved
   calibration. For a new calibration, follow the Direct Multipoint
   Calibration procedure in [SOP-L203](SOP-L203-trilogy-fluorometer.qmd),
   Section 7.3.
5. Run a 90% acetone blank
6. Wipe the outside of each cuvette with a Kimwipe before inserting
   into the fluorometer
7. Measure and record the pre-acidification fluorescence ($F_b$)

::: {.callout-note}
If the chlorophyll *a* reading exceeds 90% of the upper limit of the
linear dynamic range (LDR = 1,000 ug/L), dilute the sample before
proceeding. For a 1:2 dilution, add 1 mL of sample to 1 mL of 90%
acetone. For a 1:100 dilution, add 50 uL of sample to 4.95 mL of 90%
acetone.
:::

8. Add 75 uL of 0.1 N HCl to the cuvette. Seal with parafilm and
   invert several times to mix. Wait 90 seconds.
9. Measure and record the post-acidification fluorescence ($F_a$)
10. Repeat for all samples, QCs, and blanks


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### Calculations

**Variables:**

- $[Std]$ = concentration of the calibration standard used (ug/L)
- $S_b$ = standard fluorescence reading before acidification
- $S_a$ = standard fluorescence reading after acidification
- $F_b$ = sample fluorescence before acidification
- $F_a$ = sample fluorescence after acidification
- $V_e$ = volume of extract (mL)
- $V_s$ = volume of sample filtered (mL)

**Equations:**

$$
AR = \frac{S_b - \text{Blank}}{S_a - \text{Blank}}
$$

$$
\text{InterpB} = [Std] \times \frac{F_b - \text{Blank}}{S_b - \text{Blank}}
$$

$$
\text{InterpA} = [Std] \times \frac{F_a - \text{Blank}}{S_b - \text{Blank}}
$$

$$
\text{Chlorophyll } a \; (\mu\text{g/L}) =
\frac{AR}{AR - 1} \times (\text{InterpB} - \text{InterpA}) \times \frac{V_e}{V_s}
$$

$$
\text{Pheophytin } a \; (\mu\text{g/L}) =
\left(AR \times \text{InterpA} - \text{InterpB}\right) \times \frac{V_e}{V_s}
$$

### QC Requirements

- Run a laboratory reagent blank (LRB) every 10--15 samples. The LRB
  should read below the calculated lower detection limit.
- QC standards should recover within +/- 20% of the known value
- Relative standard deviation (RSD) of replicate measurements should be
  within +/- 20%
- Field duplicates should agree within +/- 20% relative percent
  difference
- Samples, standards, LRBs, and QCs must all be at ambient room
  temperature during analysis. Fluorescence is temperature-dependent;
  cooler samples produce artificially high readings.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Acetone extracts and rinses   | Collect in the designated organic waste bottle in the fume hood; EH&S pickup |
| Acidified sample waste (HCl)  | Add to the organic waste bottle (small volumes of dilute HCl in acetone matrix) |
| Used GF/F filters             | Standard trash (if non-hazardous samples) |
| Used cuvettes                 | Rinse with acetone, then DI water; reuse or recycle |

## Training Record

Before performing chlorophyll analysis independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L203 Trilogy Fluorometer](SOP-L203-trilogy-fluorometer.qmd),
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
   in full
2. Review the SDS for acetone and HCl
3. Demonstrate proper filtration technique under supervision
4. Perform at least one complete extraction-through-analysis cycle on
   QC standards with acceptable recovery (+/- 20%)
5. Demonstrate proper fluorometer calibration
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager


## Appendix A: Example Calculation {.appendix}

```{r}
#| label: chlorophyll-calc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

# Corrected chlorophyll a and pheophytin a calculation
# Per EPA Method 445.0

# Calibration standard
Std_conc <- 50       # ug/L (QC standard concentration)
S_b <- 485           # Standard fluorescence before acid
S_a <- 210           # Standard fluorescence after acid
blank <- 5           # Blank fluorescence

# Sample readings
F_b <- 320           # Sample fluorescence before acid
F_a <- 140           # Sample fluorescence after acid

# Volumes
V_e <- 25            # mL of extract (acetone)
V_s <- 100           # mL of sample filtered

# Calculations
AR <- (S_b - blank) / (S_a - blank)
InterpB <- Std_conc * (F_b - blank) / (S_b - blank)
InterpA <- Std_conc * (F_a - blank) / (S_b - blank)

chl_a <- (AR / (AR - 1)) * (InterpB - InterpA) * (V_e / V_s)
pheo_a <- (AR * InterpA - InterpB) * (V_e / V_s)

cat(sprintf("Acid ratio (AR):        %.3f\n", AR))
cat(sprintf("Chlorophyll a:          %.2f ug/L\n", chl_a))
cat(sprintf("Pheophytin a:           %.2f ug/L\n", pheo_a))
```


## Appendix B: Interferences {.appendix}

| Interference                  | Effect                                    | Mitigation                                |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Chlorophyll *b*               | Overestimates chlorophyll *a*             | Optical filters in the Chlor-A module minimize this; if severe, use HPLC |
| Pheophytin *a*                | Overestimates chlorophyll *a* if not acidified | Acidification step corrects for this    |
| Other fluorescent compounds   | Positive bias                             | Laboratory reagent blanks detect this     |
| Quenching (concentrated samples) | Underestimates concentration           | Dilute samples approaching 90% of LDR    |
| Temperature differences       | Higher sensitivity at lower temperatures  | Ensure all materials are at ambient temperature |
| Light exposure                 | Degrades pigments                        | Work in subdued light; wrap in foil       |
